ranked.headline: Biomolecular prediction shifts toward learned priors and coarse representations
ranked.summary: Open-source models claim to exceed AlphaFold 3, while DEL-trained and coarse-prior models test generalization without full atomic input.

ranked.headline: Deep models infer tissue organization from spatial transcriptomics and imaging
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend spatial-omics deep learning to super-resolution, pathology-omics fusion, and cross-species immune foundation models.

ranked.headline: Learned models forecast cell state transitions and perturbation responses
ranked.summary: Models are moving from static prediction toward forecasting trajectories and benchmarked simulation of single-cell and regulatory behavior.

ranked.headline: Machine learning predicts peptide, enzyme, and cyclization properties from sequence
ranked.summary: Transfer learning, geometric deep learning, and standardized benchmarks are now applied to peptide, enzyme, and cyclization prediction.

ranked.headline: Pipelines convert raw microbial measurements into interpretable biological calls
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published pipeline address error correction and reproducibility in amplicon, metagenomic, metabolomic, and genomic microbial analyses.

ranked.headline: Scalable EM and deep learning methods for genotype, splice, and methylation inference
ranked.summary: Biobank-scale and single-cell datasets are driving demand for inference methods that combine runtime efficiency with accuracy on incomplete or pooled data.

ranked.headline: QTL and GWAS methods link noncoding variants to disease genes and targets
ranked.summary: Diverse-population and multi-omic QTL datasets are sharpening variant-to-gene inference for complex trait and drug target discovery.

ranked.headline: Genome-wide sequence data inferring admixture, introgression, and population history
ranked.summary: Genome-wide sequence data now resolve admixture, archaic introgression, and early diverged human variation across dog and human populations.

ranked.headline: Sequencing error and rate variation are modeled explicitly in genomic inference
ranked.summary: Pandemic-scale viral genomics now models sequencing errors and mutation rate variation rather than treating them as preprocessing.

ranked.headline: Sequence language models are judged on structural similarity and antigenic change outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report faster tokenization, distillation and genomic architectures, now evaluated against structural similarity and antigenic outcomes.

ranked.headline: Learned models with explicit error control replace dataset-specific tuning in MS omics
ranked.summary: Mass-spectrometry omics identification and quantitation increasingly rely on learned models and FDR-controlled inference instead of raw acquisition alone.

ranked.headline: Pretrained biological encoders are probed for interpretable, residue-level structure
ranked.summary: Protein language model internals are now being dissected mechanistically while embeddings are coupled to residue-level binding and interaction outputs.

ranked.headline: Long-read and single-cell workflows resolve isoforms, splicing defects, and data artifacts
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell RNA-seq methods now quantify isoforms at cell resolution and expose empty-droplet artifacts that bias expression profiles.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic evolution models used to infer protein structure and functional constraints
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test generative and mechanistic evolution models against synthetic and alignment-level data to probe protein structure.

ranked.headline: Null-model scoring recovers multi-way co-localization and enhancer hub structure
ranked.summary: Permutation and null-model frameworks now score multi-element relationships in single-cell, spatial, and chromatin data beyond pairwise correlation.

ranked.headline: Platforms integrate omics, sequencing, and biochemical data for reproducible access
ranked.summary: Preprints from February 2026 address structuring, integrating, and querying heterogeneous omics and biochemical data locally and reproducibly.

ranked.headline: Embedding haplotype, chromatin and clonal structure into genomic inference models
ranked.summary: Single-cell, cfDNA and haplotype-resolved sequencing now pair large datasets with inference that respects biological structure.

ranked.headline: Supervised inference of pathogen resistance and identity from sequence and spectral data
ranked.summary: Recent items pair sequence- and spectra-based classifiers with curated reference sets, enabling feature-level interpretation and standardized benchmarking.

ranked.headline: New simulation and analysis software spans epidemic, neural and molecular models
ranked.summary: Four items dated February 2026 report new interfaces, packaging and cross-validation for simulation software across three fields.

ranked.headline: Model formulation choices shape inferred tumor, metabolic, and developmental biology
ranked.summary: New tumor, metabolic, and developmental models make explicit how formulation choices shape inferred biology.

ranked.headline: ML on harmonized single-cell atlases nominates disease targets and cell states
ranked.summary: Large harmonized single-cell atlases of patient tissue now support ML ranking of IBD targets, SLE rare cells, and aging-linked hematopoietic states.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics links lineage-specific gene evolution to traits across animal taxa
ranked.summary: Recent chromosome-level and synteny-aware comparative genomes attribute trait-linked gene evolution to specific lineages across diverse taxa.

ranked.headline: Compressed feature spaces are used to classify and curate cryo-EM particles
ranked.summary: Recent work applies PCA-compressed alignment and point-cloud descriptors to particle classification and curation in cryo-EM and cryo-ET.

ranked.headline: Supervised models infer latent biological state from molecular and clinical data
ranked.summary: Penalized regression, neural, and tabular foundation models now predict age, post-mortem interval, and cancer from methylation and metabolomic data.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic models map bistability, hysteresis and state transitions in cell regulation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method link gene regulatory and host-circuit dynamics to cancer cell fate and single-cell state transitions.

ranked.headline: Computational methods link noncoding and epigenetic variation to regulatory function
ranked.summary: Machine learning and deep learning models now score noncoding and epigenetic variants against chromatin, methylation and RNA modification data.

ranked.headline: Statistical tools for power, differential expression and batch effects in omics
ranked.summary: Expression studies increasingly need rigorous power estimates, Type I error control and batch-effect assessment before and after analysis.

ranked.headline: Structure-constrained learned representations for medical and microscopy imaging
ranked.summary: Four February 2026 preprints embed topological, generative, anatomical, or compression priors into biomedical imaging models.

ranked.headline: AI and network models nominate delivery proteins and SARS-CoV-2 immune biomarkers
ranked.summary: Computational screens increasingly carry predictions into validation, spanning mRNA delivery proteins to SARS-CoV-2 exposure biomarkers.

ranked.headline: Statistical tools infer population size, motif enrichment and microbiome disease models
ranked.summary: February 2026 releases extend feature-based inference to population-genetic parameters and compositional microbiome modeling, beyond element-centric prediction.

ranked.headline: LLMs as reasoning and agentic components in drug discovery workflows
ranked.summary: Evaluation of agentic and reasoning-augmented LLMs is emerging alongside systems for molecule optimization and modular discovery workflows.

ranked.headline: Restructured algorithms speed phylogenetic placement, RNA folding and graph alignment
ranked.summary: Large reference trees, pangenome graphs and mtDNA datasets demand inference methods whose cost scales sub-linearly or near-linearly.

ranked.headline: Graph and agent models predict perturbation, metabolic, and resistance biology
ranked.summary: Graph-structured and agent-based frameworks now report gains on unseen perturbation, resistance, and diagnosis prediction from limited or heterogeneous data.

ranked.headline: In silico tools map conjugated metabolites and standardize metabolomics annotation
ranked.summary: Public MS/MS archives and benchmarked prediction tools now enable systematic conjugated-metabolite mapping and metadata harmonization.

ranked.headline: Functional and network models are assigning significance to uncertain genetic variants
ranked.summary: Scalable variant calibration and gene-disease network scores target VUS reclassification and rare disease diagnosis.

ranked.headline: Noise-robust computational readouts from retinal, brain, and astrocyte imaging data
ranked.summary: Open-source and openly released tools now convert fundus, fMRI, diffusion MRI, and Ca2+ imaging data into defined quantitative biomarkers.

ranked.headline: Simulations resolve membrane binding, RNA delivery, and enzymatic free-energy barriers
ranked.summary: Recent MD and QM/MM studies assign explicit free-energy and binding-mode resolution to membrane-associated and enzymatic states.

ranked.headline: Modeling how actin feedback and active-passive interfaces shape invasive cell behavior
ranked.summary: Recent preprints model how actin feedback, tissue interfaces, and active cell mechanics drive shape changes and collective invasion.

ranked.headline: Browser-based platforms package AI molecular design and simulation workflows
ranked.summary: Molecular design and simulation workflows are being deployed as cloud-based, open-source, and zero-code software to lower barriers to access.
